# /kav-chapter <NN> — write and draw one chapter

You are the author's co-writer on chapter `<NN>` of `stories/<slug>/`. Input: the kickoff package (locked `story.md`, the chapter's `storyboard/chNN.md` card, cast / locations / objects / style). Output: `chapters/chNN/` — outline, scene plan, panels, lettering, pages, readers. Same working method as kickoff: file-persisted, gates at creative decisions, tight replies.

## Step 0 — Load context (silently)

1. `stories/<slug>/story.md` — the contract: format and panel format, telling register, POV rules, theme, feel line, curves, O/I grid
2. `stories/<slug>/storyboard/chNN.md` — this chapter's card
3. Cast DNA (`cast/<name>.md`, including Voice and Relationships) for every active character; the location docs for its sets; `style/style.md` including the lettering theme and any per-chapter imposition
4. `docs/know-how/story-craft.md` — run the checks on every scene before presenting
5. `docs/know-how/image-prompting.md` — the prompting manual for the drawing stages
6. The previous chapter's `chapters/ch(NN-1)/panels/plan.md` and pages if they exist — continuity in, guns out
7. **If `chapters/chNN/` exists: resume.** Read `chapter-state.md`, report stage statuses in a few lines, ask where to go.

If there are several stories, identify the active one from the author or from the most recently updated `kickoff-state.md` (ask if ambiguous). If the chapter card is missing or stale, stop: that is a kickoff conversation. Offer `/kav-kickoff <slug>`.

New chapter: scaffold `chapters/chNN/` with `panels/{candidates,reviews,lettering}/`, `pages/`, and `chapter-state.md` from `docs/templates.md`.

**Costs are recorded as they happen.** Every generation appends a row to `stories/<slug>/ledger.jsonl` — model, stage, price, outcome — including rerolls and takes nobody picks. When a chapter closes, `python3 tools/ledger.py --story <slug>` gives the running total; quote it as a documented minimum, never as the provider's bill.

**Say where the author is, at every gate.** A chapter runs **outline → picks → lettering → review → publish**, and every message that asks for a decision opens with the one-line progress header (`docs/know-how/progress.md`): story, chapter, step, and how much of the book is done. Update the Progress block in `kickoff-state.md` as each step closes. A chapter is finished when it is **published** and the author can read it on a phone — not when the panels are lettered.

## Stage A — Outline, in content (GATE)

Open with the chapter **in content, not process**. Three short parts:

> **In the last chapter** <what concretely happened — events, not themes>.
> **In this one** <what happens, in one or two sentences>.
> **The suggested plot:**
> 1. <a concrete scene: who, where, what they do>
> 2. …
> n. …

Concrete scenes a reader would see — never arc philosophising, curve talk or craft vocabulary in this message. The craft checks run *before* you present (one-sentence test, press, curve placement, gun ledger against the card); they show up as a better list, not as commentary. If a check fails in a way the author must decide, say so in one line under the list.

The author redirects, cuts, adds or reorders. Iterate until they agree.

## Stage B — Scene list → `panels/plan.md` (GATE)

Expand the agreed plot into a scene list. One scene = one strip. Per scene:

```
## S<k> · <short title>
**Set:** <location>, <time>. **Present:** <who>.
<2–5 lines: what happens, in the story language; the exact text proposals —
captions, balloons, thoughts, sounds — inline>
*<N> panels — <shape per panel: 1/2/3 cells>.*
```

Plan panels per scene within the card's layout budget. A panel is **one drawable frozen moment**, not a summary.

**Plan panels to the selected model's reference budget.** Read it before planning: the story's lock in `style/style.md`, else `KAV_PROVIDER` in `.env`, else what `python3 tools/check_setup.py` reports. Every character and every bound object takes a reference slot ahead of the style pack, so the budget sets how many subjects a panel can name — **three on a capped provider like Magnific (5 images)**; on fal.ai the stack is bigger, but a fourth face still drifts first. Write beats that fit: the fourth character is in the next panel, in the background unnamed, or seen from behind.

When the author asks for a panel that crosses it, say it plainly and early, in the room's language: *"On Magnific we can't put more than three cast members and objects in one panel. For a scene like that we'd have to switch to another image provider."* Then offer the two ways out — split the panel, or switch the provider — and do as they say. Save the mechanism (reference slots, the style pack losing its images) for when they ask why. The tools print the same warning if one slips through. Under a different lock the number changes, so re-read it rather than quoting this one. Shot size follows the cell count: wide establishing = 3 cells, mid = 2, close = 1. For the Instagram-master format, rows on a page sum to 3 cells; a scene may end mid-row so the next scene closes it.

**Present the list and wait.** Then, when it is approved, **go straight to the images** — don't stop again to confirm that you are about to generate what was just agreed. "Proceed" means: do the work and come back with the takes to pick from. The author cuts panels ("it added nothing"), merges scenes, rewrites beats. Record every cut in `plan.md` as a one-line italic note so the history stays readable. Script changes after images exist mark the affected panels stale.

## Stage C — Panels: batch → review page → picks in

### 1 · Write the batch

One batch per 2–4 scenes: `chapters/chNN/panels/batch-<name>.json`

```json
{
  "story": "<slug>",
  "chapter": "chNN",
  "lane": "seedream",
  "n": 3,
  "panels": [
    {"id": "s1p1", "ar": "4:5",  "line": "<scene line naming cast + location words>", "text": "caption: …\nmira (thought): …"},
    {"id": "s1p2", "ar": "8:5",  "line": "…", "text": "…"},
    {"id": "s2p1", "ar": "4:5",  "picked": "2", "text": "…"}
  ]
}
```

- `n` = **2–4 takes per panel**. Explore on the cheap lane (Seedream); move a panel to Nano Banana only when it needs what that lane does better (text in frame, a recognisable real place, a precise gesture) — see `docs/know-how/image-prompting.md`.
- `ar` from the cell count: 1 cell = `4:5`, 2 cells = `8:5`, 3 cells = `12:5`.
- `line` follows the prompting manual: name every cast member present (that's how references bind), use the location's trigger words, name the specific place first, frame positively, give the subject a position ("in the foreground centre, face clear"). Never put dialogue in the line. For a wide panel, keep the subject in the centre third of the frame. Leave negative space where the text will go.
- `text` carries the proposed lettering so the author can edit it on the review page.
- A panel already settled carries `"picked": "<take>"` — it renders locked (its chosen image only, still open for text edits) so one page covers a mixed round of rerolls and text passes.

**Prove the binding before paying for the batch** (first batch of a chapter, and after any change to `briefs.json`, the pack or the lane):

```
python3 tools/panel_batch.py chapters/chNN/panels/batch-<name>.json --preflight
```

It resolves one panel without generating and prints the style, the reference counts, the `medium.txt` line and the prompt. A locked `style/style.md` and a linked `styles/<pack>/` bind nothing by themselves — the pack reaches the prompt only from `defaults.style_pack` in `briefs.json`, the scene line, or `--style`. If it says `style=NONE`, fix `briefs.json` before generating; a batch run without a style is a chapter of the model's own look. Then generate **one proof panel** (`n: 1`, one id in `"only"`), look at it, and only then run the batch:

```
python3 tools/panel_batch.py chapters/chNN/panels/batch-<name>.json
```

Candidates land in `panels/candidates/<id>-<take>.png` with a `.json` sidecar naming what bound. The tool refuses to call a batch clean when any candidate came back with no style bound; those are a failed batch, not options — never put them in front of the author.

### 2 · Open the review page

**Use the author's review surface** (`KAV_REVIEW`, see `docs/know-how/review-surfaces.md`):

- **`inline`** — post the batch's contact sheet (`panels/candidates/<batch-stem>_sheet.png`, every take burned in as `<id> A/B/C`) and take the picks by name: "s2p1 B". Apply them by writing `panels/reviews/<batch-stem>.json` yourself, in the same shape the page saves.
- **`artifact`** — publish the same board as a page and share the link.
- **`local`** — `python3 tools/review.py <batch.json>`, or `/kav-review <batch.json>`: **the full chapter in reading order**, locked picks shown as their chosen image, open panels showing every take with the full image and its phone crop side by side, click to pick, reroll with a note, edit the caption text; one save writes `panels/reviews/<batch-stem>.json`. Post the contact sheet as well — a page on `127.0.0.1` is invisible from a phone or a hosted session.

Then tell the author what is waiting and stop. **The author picks every image.**

### 3 · Picks in

When the author says the picks are in, read `panels/reviews/<batch-stem>.json` and apply it:
- **picks** → record in `panels/manifest.md` (panel → scene → line → chosen file) and in the next batch as `"picked"`.
- **rerolls** → rewrite the line **for the named reason** and regenerate only those panels. Reroll on a reason with a changed line, never the same line again: "wrong direction" → move the camera; a character lost in a crowd → "in the foreground centre, close to the camera, face clear" plus the identity words repeated; a real place → bind its photo and keep the place name out of the line (it becomes signage); "neon" → "tube light, no signs, no lettering".
- **text edits** → the author's lines replace your proposals **verbatim** (fix obvious typos and flag them). Proposals are scaffolding.
- **notes** → act on them or ask.

Repeat review rounds until every panel in the chapter is picked.

### Continuity — by reference, not by prompt

- **When a place drifts** (a room grows, a door becomes a gate, a ceiling vanishes), don't fight it with adjectives. Copy an **approved earlier panel** of that place into `locations/<name>/` and add it to the location's `photos` in `briefs.json` — the next generation binds the *drawn* place. The same for a prop that must stay identical (or promote it to an object).
- **When a place comes out wrong, check what actually bound before rewriting the line.** The sidecar `.json` beside every candidate names the bound location. Location words are first-match: a generic word ("apartment") in one location's triggers can steal a scene meant for another. Fix the vocabulary, not only the prose.
- Same character across panels = same reference set. Drift is a bug: regenerate, don't accept.
- A picked image whose shape is wrong gets cropped with `python3 tools/cell_crop.py <image> --cells 1|2|3`, not regenerated — the author's pick is the composition.

## Stage D — Lettering (post-process, never in generation)

Story text is never generated into the image. **Never letter an unpicked image.** For each picked panel, **look at the image first**, then write `panels/lettering/pNN-panelK.json` and render:

```
python3 tools/letter.py panels/lettering/pNN-panelK.json panels/pNN-panelK.png
python3 tools/letter.py panels/lettering/pNN-panelK.json panels/pNN-panelK.phone.png --phone   # wide panels
```

Spec shape (see the tool's examples in `tools/examples/`):

```json
{
  "story": "<slug>",
  "panel": "chapters/chNN/panels/candidates/s1p1-2.png",
  "size": [2304, 2880],
  "style": {"caption": {"fill": "#1b2740", "color": "#f4ecd6", "size": 76}},
  "overlays": [
    {"type": "caption", "x": 60, "y": 50, "w": 2184, "h": 220, "lang": "he", "lines": ["…"]},
    {"type": "thought", "cx": 1500, "cy": 700, "rx": 420, "ry": 180, "target": [1200, 1400], "lines": ["…"]},
    {"type": "shout", "cx": 1700, "cy": 300, "rx": 380, "ry": 160, "lines": ["…"]}
  ]
}
```

### Lettering rules

- **Who speaks how** (defaults — the story's declared register in `story.md` overrides):
  - Third person about the protagonist, the narrator's voice = **caption**.
  - The protagonist thinking = **thought bubble**.
  - Other characters **speak little** — short speech balloons, small vocabulary.
  - **Sounds** — growls, sirens, alarms, howls, off-panel yelling = **burst** (`shout`), big. Ownerless crowd chatter = tailless bursts.
  - Caption = narrator register, balloon = character register. They never blur.
- **A balloon never ends on a period.** Balloons are speech and thought, not prose. Mid-line punctuation stays; ellipses, question marks, exclamation marks and emoji stand. Captions are the narrator and keep normal punctuation.
- **Captions are full-width, right-aligned bands** for right-to-left languages (left-aligned for left-to-right), across the top or bottom of the panel, not boxes floating in corners.
- **Every balloon and caption sits inside the phone-safe zone.** The phone crop of a wide panel is its centre 4:5. For 8:5 that is the **middle half**, x 25%..75% of the full width (3456 wide → x 864..2592); for 12:5 it is the **middle third**, x 33%..67% (3840 wide → x 1280..2560). `python3 tools/cell_crop.py <image> --cells 2|3` prints the exact bounds. Check `cx ± rx` and caption `x..x+w` against those bounds before rendering. A caption band on a wide panel spans only the safe zone, or gets a separate `--phone` render.
- **Wide panels get a phone render** (`--phone`) so the story reader shows lettering sized for the crop.
- Never cover a face; prefer background over bodies. Tails point at the speaker's mouth and stop short of the head.
- Reading order = vertical order: earlier text sits higher. When two overlays share a height, the earlier one goes right in RTL, left in LTR.
- Balloon text stays short: two tight lines. Longer means split it or move it to a caption.
- Emoji are legal in balloons, a character-voice choice — sparingly, never carrying plot.

### Verify — mandatory

Look at every rendered PNG (and phone render). Check: no balloon over a face · captions and balloons not colliding · tails aimed right · reading order clear · text fits with air around it · everything inside the phone-safe zone. Fix the spec and re-render until clean. Never hand the author unverified lettering; a collision the author finds is a bug in the loop.

## Stage E — Pages, carousel, readers (GATE)

1. Write `pages/layout.json` — each page's rows as `[panel-id, cells]` **in reading order**. For a right-to-left story the first panel of a row is placed at the right edge (the tool handles RTL when the story language is RTL; say so in the layout if the tool expects a flag):

```json
{"story": "<slug>", "chapter": "chNN", "page_width": 2400, "gutter": 36,
 "pages": [{"id": "p01", "rows": [[["p01-panel1", 1], ["p01-panel2", 2]], [["p01-panel3", 3]]]}]}
```

2. `python3 tools/assemble.py pages/layout.json` → `pages/pNN.png` plus `pages/carousel/NN-<panel>.jpg` (every panel as a 1080×1350 image, wide panels cropped to their centre safe zone).
3. **Look at the pages and the carousel crops**, not just the pages — a balloon that clears the page can still be clipped on the phone.
4. Build the two readers:

```
python3 tools/build_readers.py --story <slug> --chapters chNN --title "<chapter title>" \
  --out stories/<slug>/chapters/chNN/pages \
  [--next "<next chapter title>"] [--next-story-url <next chapter reader-story.html>] \
  [--next-pages-url <next chapter reader-comic.html>] [--home-url <trailer or story home>]
```

- **Story** reader (`reader-story.html`) — one panel per screen, phone first. **Comic** reader (`reader-comic.html`) — the assembled pages top to bottom.
- Navigation like a phone story: swipe or tap a side; nothing types, fills or waits.
- One title screen per chapter: the story name small above, the chapter name big below.
- The last screen links to the next chapter **in the same mode** (story → story, comic → comic); a chapter without a next one closes on its last line. Every reader links back home (the trailer deck or the story's index).
- When you finish chapter NN, rebuild chapter NN-1's readers with `--next-*` pointing here.

**GATE on the chapter:** the author reads it end to end in a reader. On lock:
- Update `chapter-state.md` and the chapter row in `kickoff-state.md` (Written ✓)
- Append this chapter's events to the locations' History and the cast's Story state
- Log unpaid guns and open questions for the next chapter
- Offer to update the trailer (`/kav-trailer`) so its chapter slide links into the readers

## Hard rules

- The kickoff package is the contract. Bend it, never contradict it without a logged decision — contradictions go back to `/kav-kickoff`.
- Outline in content first; scene list gate before any image is generated.
- Every scene passes the one-sentence test before the author sees it. DNA ≠ I/O.
- **The author picks every image that lands in a page**, on the review page. Never promote a pick the author didn't make.
- Never letter an unpicked image. Lettering is always post-process, always verified by looking.
- The author's text replaces proposals verbatim.
- Story scope: every tool call carries `--story <slug>` or a story-local batch; nothing reads from or writes to another story.
- Persist every step; track staleness across stages; never absorb silently.
- Never publish anywhere outside the repo without asking.
